run.question:
payment-service is throwing 500 errors — investigate the root cause using
the app-263-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The index app-263-prod-logs exists and holds exactly 7 documents, all of which fall inside the authorized window (timestamps 2026-11-21T04:10:16Z to 2026-11-21T05:40:16Z). Its only service label values are payment-service-us (3 docs), payment-service-ap (2) and payment-service-eu (2); there is no document for an exact service named 'payment-service', and a query for message text '500'/'Internal Server Error' returned no documents at all, so HTTP 500 status codes are not observed in this index (only generic ERROR/WARN application lines). The observed errors point outward and differ per shard: payment-service-eu logged 'adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable' (04:10:16Z) and then 'Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key' (05:10:16Z), while payment-service-us logged 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us after 30000ms' (04:10:16Z), 'Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)' (05:10:16Z) and WARN 'Retry queue depth=812' (05:40:16Z); payment-service-ap logged only INFO 'Healthy' lines. So the deepest supported reading is a hypothesis, not an observed mechanism: upstream provider failures (adyen-eu credential rejection; stripe-us 30s timeouts with consequent connection-pool exhaustion and retry backlog) are the most likely origins of the payment-service error logs. Important scoping caveat: the logs carry no cluster/region field, and the only Kubernetes cluster I can read (production-eu-west-2, data source otel-demo, target m0-otel-20260909) contains no workload named payment-service*; its only payment workload is Deployment otel-demo/payment, whose pod is ready, whose keyword-filtered logs contained no application error lines, and whose flagd fault-injection flags paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable are both defined with defaultVariant 'off'. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable for every attempt in this Run, so no error-rate, latency baseline or trace/call-chain evidence exists; the claimed 500s and the exact trigger of the adyen-eu api_key rejection remain unverified.

claims.text: app-263-prod-logs is the only index in the Elasticsearch data source (docs.count 7, green), and a timestamp-sorted retrieval over the full authorized window returned all 7 documents with timestamps from 2026-11-21T04:10:16Z to 2026-11-21T05:40:16Z.

In app-263-prod-logs over the authorized window the service label buckets are payment-service-us (3 docs), payment-service-ap (2 docs) and payment-service-eu (2 docs); level buckets are ERROR 4, INFO 2, WARN 1. No other service value was observed.
payment-service-eu logged ERROR 'adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable' at 2026-11-21T04:10:16Z.
payment-service-eu logged ERROR 'Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key' at 2026-11-21T05:10:16Z.

payment-service-us logged ERROR 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us after 30000ms' at 2026-11-21T04:10:16Z, ERROR 'Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)' at 2026-11-21T05:10:16Z and WARN 'Retry queue depth=812' at 2026-11-21T05:40:16Z.

payment-service-ap logged only INFO lines in the window: 'Healthy: p95 latency 290ms' at 2026-11-21T04:10:16Z and 'Healthy' at 2026-11-21T05:40:16Z; no ERROR or WARN document from this shard was observed.

In the readable cluster production-eu-west-2 (data source otel-demo, target m0-otel-20260909) no Deployment, Service or Pod named payment-service* exists; the only payment workload is Deployment otel-demo/payment (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment, 1/1 available and ready, env FLAGD_HOST=flagd) and the only payment Service is otel-demo/payment on port 8080. The log service names payment-service-us/eu/ap therefore do not correspond to any workload visible in this cluster.

The otel-demo payment pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d (owner ReplicaSet payment-6f7bc865d6, started 2026-11-20T16:32:07Z) is Running and its single container is ready with restartCount 1; its previous container instance terminated at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z with exitCode 255 and reason 'Unknown'.

A keyword-filtered read (err|error|exception|fail|panic|timeout|refus) of pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d covering 2026-11-21T03:50:00Z-06:10:00Z, across both the current and the previous container instance (413 lines read), returned exactly one matching line: '(node:24) MetadataLookupWarning: received unexpected error = Invalid response from metadata service: incorrect Metadata-Flavor header. code = UNKNOWN' at 2026-11-21T04:23:52.607241329Z; no application-level error line from the payment container was returned.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config defines the fault-injection flags paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'), both with state ENABLED and defaultVariant 'off'; the other flags in that ConfigMap (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) also have defaultVariant 'off'.

The only events inside the authorized window group to namespace app-101 (Pod Created/Killing/Pulled/Scheduled/Started, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, Deployment ScalingReplicaSet) plus one Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint event ('Failed to create endpoint for service app-282/loki: endpoints "loki" already exists', 05:28:04Z); no event involves otel-demo or any payment object.

The most likely origin of the payment-service errors is its upstream payment providers rather than the payment application itself: adyen-eu rejecting payment-service-eu's credential ('invalid api_key', preceded by an adyen-eu 503) and stripe-us exceeding a 30s call timeout toward payment-service-us, with 'Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)' and 'Retry queue depth=812' as consequences of that upstream slowness. This chain is inferred from the log lines only; no 500 status, metric or span was observed for these services.

A second, not-excluded candidate is local capacity/config exhaustion in payment-service-us: the pool ceiling stated in the log is max=50 with active=50, so pool sizing or connection lease handling (not only stripe-us latency) may independently produce failures, and the rising retry queue (depth=812) may amplify them. No metric or trace was available to separate these two candidates.

Rejected as an explanation for the payment-service errors: fault injection through the cluster's flagd payment flags. Both paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable are defined with defaultVariant 'off' in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config, they govern the otel-demo/payment workload (a different entity than payment-service-*), and that workload's pod logs returned no application error lines. No object applying a payment fault to payment-service-us/eu/ap was observed.

The claim that the cluster's payment workload is failing is not supported: the only payment workload present, Deployment otel-demo/payment, reports 1/1 ready and available replicas with condition Available (MinimumReplicasAvailable, lastTransitionTime 2026-11-20T16:33:03Z), and its pod's current instance is ready. This concerns a different entity than the payment-service-* names in the log index.

Verify and rotate the adyen-eu API credential used by payment-service-eu (its own logs state 'invalid api_key'), and compare the credential version/timestamp with the 05:10:16Z error; secret values could not be read in this Run, so the key's current value and change time must be checked by a human with secret access.

For payment-service-us, correlate stripe-us provider latency/error rates with the 30s timeout setting and review the pool ceiling (max=50) and retry-queue handling, since pool exhaustion and a retry backlog are the observable consequences; restore Prometheus/Jaeger reachability first so the error ratio and call chain can be measured instead of inferred.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable for every attempt in this Run (get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query twice, metrics_range_query, get_prometheus_target all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no traces_span_metrics_calls_total error ratio, no rpc/http latency series and no comparable latency baseline exist; the claimed 500 status codes and any latency trend are unmeasured.

Jaeger was unavailable for every attempt (traces_list_services and traces_search for service 'payment' both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so there are no spans, no observed parent-child call edges, and no independent confirmation of which upstream calls the payment services made.

No document in app-263-prod-logs has service exactly 'payment-service', and the exact-name plus message-phrase query (service=payment-service OR message contains '500' OR 'Internal Server Error') returned zero documents (view status no_data, not citable); the specific HTTP 500 the question describes is not visible in this index, and the three observed names payment-service-us/eu/ap are different entities from that exact name.

app-263-prod-logs carries only the fields level, message, service and timestamp: there is no cluster, region or environment field, so I could not verify which cluster/environment these payment-service-* logs belong to, and no workload with those names exists in the readable cluster production-eu-west-2.

Secrets cannot be read, and the change_history integration is not available in this Run, so the actual adyen-eu api_key value, when it changed, and whether a credential rotation coincided with the 05:10:16Z error could not be verified.

The otel-demo payment container's previous instance terminated with exitCode 255 and reason 'Unknown' at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z; no log line or event explains the restart, and no evidence ties it to the payment-service-* log errors, so its trigger remains unknown (recorded as a gap, not as impact).

Deployment payment-api-101 in namespace app-101 was scaled from 0 to 1 at 2026-11-21T06:06:06Z (ReplicaSet payment-api-101-8486559b69 created pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-v4v9b) and no such deployment or pod exists at query time; its role and relation to the app-263-prod-logs index could not be determined.

Kubernetes object state and the single event listing were read at ~06:10Z, after the incident window's end; they cannot prove what the cluster looked like at 04:10-05:40Z, and absence of events for otel-demo is unknown rather than proof.
next_steps: Restore Prometheus and Jaeger connectivity and re-run the error-ratio and latency queries for the payment services (also confirming which cluster/region their series and traces carry) to measure whether 500s coincide with the 04:10-05:40Z log lines.
Have a human with secret access check the adyen-eu API key version and rotation history for payment-service-eu, and confirm the adyen-eu 503 at 04:10:16Z against the provider's status history.
Review payment-service-us connection-pool sizing (max=50) and retry-queue behaviour, and compare stripe-us provider latency against the 30s call timeout.

Confirm the cluster/region attribution of the app-263-prod-logs documents (its writer's environment) before using them for any production-eu-west-2 decision, since no workload named payment-service-* exists in that cluster.

Explain or acknowledge the otel-demo/payment container restart at 04:23:42Z (exitCode 255, reason Unknown) and the transient app-101 deployment payment-api-101, so they are neither ignored nor mistaken for impact.

data.alertmanager.yml:
global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:
        [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] /etc/alertmanager/opspilot/token
        type: Bearer [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] ${env:PROMETHEUS_COLLECTOR_PASSWORD}
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000

    - __meta_kubernetes_namespace
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_name
    - __meta_kubernetes_endpoint_port_name
  scheme: https
  tls_config:
    ca_file: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt
- bearer_token_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
  job_name: kubernetes-nodes
  kubernetes_sd_configs:

  relabel_configs:
  - action: labelmap
    regex: __meta_kubernetes_node_label_(.+)
  - replacement: kubernetes.default.svc:443
    target_label: __address__
  - regex: (.+)
    replacement: /api/v1/nodes/$1/proxy/metrics
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_node_name
    target_label: __metrics_path__
  scheme: https
  tls_config:
    ca_file: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt

  alertmanagers:

      - targets:

data.alerting_rules.yml:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical

Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
